question.text: 'Saraswati Growth Fund' recovers INR 40 crore from an early exit within the investment period. The PPM has an explicit 'recycling' clause. What does this mean for the LPs?

answer.text: The fund must distribute the INR 40 crore immediately - no re-deployment permitted.
SEBI requires the INR 40 crore to be parked in G-Secs until fund winding up.
The manager may re-deploy the INR 40 crore into new investments, effectively reusing capital within the investment period as per PPM conditions.
LPs automatically receive a waiver on future drawdowns equal to INR 40 crore.

explanation.text: The Logic: A 'recycling' or 're-investment' clause in a PE fund's PPM/LPA allows the manager to redeploy capital returned from an early exit into new investments within the commitment/investment period, subject to caps and conditions in the PPM (commonly tied to the type of proceeds, the time elapsed, and a percentage-of-commitments cap). Without such a clause, the returned proceeds must be distributed to LPs. The Trap: 'Distribute immediately' is the default behaviour ONLY when there is no recycling clause. SEBI does not require parking in G-Secs. Drawdown waivers are not the consequence of a recycling clause. Note: The XIX-D workbook references return of drawdown subject to recall and discusses drawdown/distribution mechanics, but does not specifically define a recycling/re-investment clause permitting early-exit redeployment. Treat recycling-clause behaviour above as general PE-LPA practice applicable when reading AIF fund documents.
